source.name: City of Calgary Open Data · Current Year Property Assessments
source.licence: Open Government Licence – City of Calgary

sources.name: raw_assessments
sources.description: Residential parcels for home property uses, as the API returns them. Every field is text.

sources.name: raw_use_codes
sources.description: The City's lookup of sub-property use codes to labels, from a second dataset.

models.name: stg_homes
models.description: Typed and labelled. Use codes joined to the City's own descriptions, zoning reduced to its primary district, and the 1800 placeholder for an unknown build year turned into NULL.
models.sql:
-- Homes only: no parking stalls, storage units, vacant land or whole rental buildings.
select
    try_cast(a.roll_number as bigint)                               as roll_number,
    try_cast(a.roll_year as integer)                                as roll_year,
    a.comm_name                                                     as community,
    a.sub_property_use                                              as use_code,
    u.description                                                   as use,
    case a.sub_property_use
        when 'R110' then 'Detached' when 'R111' then 'Detached'
        when 'R120' then 'Duplex'
        when 'R401' then 'Townhouse' when 'R402' then 'Townhouse'
        when 'R201' then 'Condo apartment' when 'R301' then 'Condo apartment'
    end                                                             as property_group,
    nullif(trim(split_part(a.land_use_designation, ',', 1)), '')    as zoning,
    -- The City records 1800 when the build year is unknown.
    nullif(try_cast(try_cast(a.year_of_construction as double) as integer), 1800) as year_built,
    try_cast(try_cast(a.land_size_sf as double) as integer)         as lot_sqft,
    try_cast(try_cast(a.assessed_value as double) as integer)       as assessed_value,
    cast(try_cast(a.mod_date as timestamp) as date)                 as mod_date
from {{ ref('raw_assessments') }} a
left join {{ ref('raw_use_codes') }} u on u.code = a.sub_property_use
qualify row_number() over (partition by a.roll_number order by a.mod_date desc) = 1

models.name: housing_homes
models.description: One row per home with its 2026 assessed value. No addresses. Served as Parquet and used to train the value model.
models.sql:
select roll_number, roll_year, community, use, property_group, zoning, year_built, lot_sqft, assessed_value, mod_date
from {{ ref('stg_homes') }}
where assessed_value > 0
order by community, roll_number

tests.name: property_group is a known value
tests.description: Only the home types the model and dashboard expect.
tests.sql:
select count(*) as failures from (
with all_values as (

    select
        property_group as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from {{ ref('housing_homes') }}
    group by property_group

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'Detached','Duplex','Townhouse','Condo apartment'
)
) dbt_test

tests.name: One assessment roll year
tests.description: Mixing two roll years would blend two years of values into one model.
tests.sql:
select count(*) as failures from (
with all_values as (

    select
        roll_year as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from {{ ref('housing_homes') }}
    group by roll_year

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    2026
)
) dbt_test

tests.name: Assessed value is plausible ($50k to $20M)
tests.description: Outliers are kept but flagged. The model trains on log value, which limits their pull.

tests.name: Year built is plausible
tests.description: Catches zeros and typos in construction year.

tests.name: roll_number is never null
tests.description: Every home is addressable for incremental merges.

tests.name: Every use code has a City label
tests.description: If the City adds a code, the join fails loudly instead of producing unlabelled homes.

tests.name: Year built is present
tests.description: Missing years are kept. The model routes missing values down their own branch.

tests.name: At least 400,000 homes
tests.description: Guards against a partial extract replacing the table and retraining the model on it.

tests.name: roll_number is unique
tests.sql:
select count(*) as failures from (
select
    roll_number as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from {{ ref('housing_homes') }}
where roll_number is not null
group by roll_number
having count(*) > 1
) dbt_test

highlights.sql:
select 1 as sort, 'Median detached home' as label, 'money' as format,
       median(assessed_value)::double as value_number, null::varchar as value_text, '2026 assessment' as detail
from {{ ref('housing_homes') }} where property_group = 'Detached'

union all

select 2, 'Homes assessed at $1M or more', 'percent',
       avg((assessed_value >= 1000000)::integer), null, 'of all homes'
from {{ ref('housing_homes') }}

union all

select * from (
    select 3, 'Highest-value community', 'text', null, community, 'by median detached value'
    from {{ ref('housing_homes') }}
    where property_group = 'Detached' and community not like 'RESIDUAL%'
    group by community having count(*) >= 50
    order by median(assessed_value) desc limit 1
)

contract.cadence: Weekly, Mondays at 10:00 UTC, via Airflow on GitHub Actions
guarantees: Values are the City's 2026 assessments (market value as of July 1, 2025), not sale prices.
Homes only: detached, duplex, townhouse and condo apartment units.
No addresses or owner details are served to the browser.
The model retrains only after every error-level test passes.

model.name: value_model
model.description: XGBoost gradient-boosted trees on log assessed value, trained in Python after the tests pass. Features: community, property type, zoning, year built, lot size.
